R1(config-if)#application redundancy rg1 hello 3
R1(config-if)#application redundancy rg1 hold 10
R1(config-if)#application redundancy rg1 auth text
R1(config-if)#bfd enable

R2(config)#interface port-channel 10
R2(config-if)#channel-group 10 mode active
R2(config-if)#exit
R2(config)#interface range Ethernet0/0-Ethernet0/2
R2(config-if-range)#channel-group 10 mode active
R2(config-if-range)#exit
R2(config)#interface GigabitEthernet0/0
R2(config-if)#ip address 10.255.20.2 255.255.255.0
R2(config-if)#exit

R3(config)#interface Port-channel1
R3(config-if)#ip address 10.255.20.3 255.255.255.0
R3(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode active
R3(config-if)#exit
R3(config)#interface Ethernet0/1
R3(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode active
R3(config-if)#exit
R3(config)#interface Ethernet0/2
R3(config-if)#channel-group 1 mode active
R3(config-if)#exit

R4(config)#ip mobile-ip home-agent
R4(config-mob-ha)#track-object 100 ip mobile-ip home-agent
R4(config-mob-ha-track)#exit

R1(config)#crypto gdoi group gdoigroupone
R1(config-gdoi-group)#group-member crypto-state tracked-object 99

R2(config-if)#interface Ethernet0/1  
R2(config-if)#ip nat outside  
R2(config-if)#ip virtual-reassembly in  
R2(config-if)#standby 200 ip 10.0.23.200  
R2(config-if)#standby 200 priority 100  
R2(config-if)#standby 200 preempt  
R2(config-if)#standby 200 group 1

R3(config)#interface nve1  
R3(config-if)#source loopback 0  
R3(config-if)#member vni 7115  
R3(config-if)#multicast-group 225.1.1.1  
R3(config-if)#no shutdown

R4(config-if)#interface Ethernet0/2  
R4(config-if)#ipv6 address 2001:DB8:2222::1/48  
R4(config-if)#ip nat outside  
R4(config-if)#zone-member security z2  
R4(config-if)#tcp mss-clamp 1360  
R4(config-if)#redundancy group 360  
R4(config-if)#redundancy asymmetric-routing

R1(config)#ip cisco-sxp-password Cisco123
R1(config)#ip cisco-sxp-source 10.255.0.1
R1(config)#ip cisco-sxp-peer 10.0.12.2 password default mode local both
R1(config)#ip cisco-sxp-speaker-hold-time 950
R1(config)#ip cisco-sxp-listener-hold-time 750 1500
R2(config-if)# ip cisco-sgt caching

retrieved_logs.requirement: On R2, which runs BGP in autonomous system 65000, allow internal BGP to install up to 3 equal-cost paths for IPv6 prefixes so traffic is load-shared across them.

On R1, create a VPN routing instance "vpn1" (route distinguisher 45000:5, importing and exporting route-target 45000:100), place interface Ethernet0/0 (10.0.1.1/24) into it, and peer with the CE 10.0.1.2 in remote AS 50000 under the IPv4 VRF address family of BGP AS 45000; activate the neighbor and cap it at 10000 prefixes in warning-only mode.
On R3 (BGP AS 45000), generate an aggregate for 10.0.0.0/8 by creating a static route for that block to null0 and redistributing static routes into BGP.
On R4 (BGP AS 45000), advertise an aggregate route for 10.0.0.0/8 and have it carry the combined AS_PATH information of the more-specific routes it summarizes.

On R1 (BGP AS 45000) peering with 10.0.12.2 in AS 40000, advertise only the aggregate 10.0.0.0/8 (hide the more-specifics), but selectively let the routes chosen by route-map map1 still be advertised to that neighbor.

On R2 (BGP AS 45000) peering with 10.0.12.1 in AS 40000, advertise the routes permitted by ACL 1 (10.0.1.0) to that neighbor only while the routes permitted by ACL 2 (10.0.2.0) are present in the BGP table.
On R3 (BGP AS 40000) peering with 10.0.23.1, inject a default route toward that neighbor, but only when 10.0.1.0/24 is present, using a route-map keyed on a prefix-list.
On R4 (BGP AS 45000) with an iBGP neighbor 10.0.24.1 in the same AS 45000, treat 10.0.20.0 as a backdoor network so the locally learned IGP path is preferred over the eBGP path.
On R1 (BGP AS 40000), create a peer group named "fingroup", make 10.0.14.2 (remote AS 45000) a member of it, and activate the peer group under the IPv4 multicast address family.
On R2 (BGP AS 45000), define a reusable peer-policy template "GLOBAL" that limits a peer to 10000 prefixes, sets a weight of 300, and applies inbound prefix-list NO-MARKETING.
On R1, bring up OSPF with process id 109 and advertise the 10.0.12.0/24 link into area 20.
On R2, under OSPF process 10 make area 10.0.0.0 a totally stubby area that uses authentication and advertises a default summary cost of 1.
On R3, under OSPF process 10 redistribute RIP (with subnets), advertise 10.0.2.0 into area 1, turn area 1 into an NSSA, and summarize 10.0.40.0/24 so it is not advertised.
On R4 (OSPF process 1), force this NSSA ABR to always translate Type-7 LSAs into Type-5 and to suppress the forwarding address in the translated LSAs for area 10.
On R1 (OSPF process 1), turn off RFC 3101 behavior and instead use the RFC 1587 method of handling NSSA areas.
On R2 (OSPF process 109), originate a default route into OSPF unconditionally, even when R2 itself has no default route.
On R3 (OSPF process 109), change the administrative distance used for OSPF external routes to 200.
On R4 (OSPF process 109), tune the SPF throttle timers to 5 ms initial delay, 1000 ms minimum hold, and 9000 ms maximum hold.
On R1 (OSPF process 109), log a detailed message every time a neighbor adjacency goes up or down.
On R2 (OSPF process 109), set the LSA group pacing interval to 60 seconds.
On R3 interface Ethernet0/0, secure OSPFv3 for IPv6 with IPsec authentication using SPI 500 and MD5 key 1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef.
On R1, enable EIGRP in autonomous system 109 and advertise the networks 10.0.1.0 and 10.0.12.0.
On R2, stop redistributing BGP AS 45000 into EIGRP AS 100 and delete the now-unused route-map "bgp-to-eigrp".
On R3, enable EIGRP in autonomous system 1 and advertise the 10.0.0.0 network.
On R4, disable automatic summarization for EIGRP AS 101, and on Ethernet0/1 advertise a manual EIGRP 100 summary for 10.0.0.0/0 and cap EIGRP 209 to 75% of the link bandwidth.
On R1, for EIGRP AS 101 set the event log buffer size to 5000010, log neighbor changes, and log neighbor warnings every 300 seconds.
On R2, for EIGRP AS 101 enable balanced unequal-cost load sharing across up to 5 paths with a variance of 1.
On R3 interface Ethernet0/2, set the EIGRP AS 109 hello interval to 10 seconds and the hold time to 40 seconds.
On R4 interface Ethernet0/1, disable split horizon for EIGRP AS 101.
On R1 interface Ethernet0/0, advertise an EIGRP for IPv6 summary address 2001:DB8:0:1::/64 for process 1.
On R2, enable RIP version 2 with automatic summarization turned off, advertising networks 10.0.12.0 and 10.0.20.0.
On R3, start an IS-IS routing process with area tag "osi-as-101", assign the NET 49.0101.1111.1111.1111.1111.00, and make it a Level-1-only router.
On R4 interface Ethernet0/0 (10.0.14.2/24), enable IS-IS IP routing and CLNS routing for the "osi-as-202" process and bring the interface up.
On R1 interface Ethernet0/0, configure IPv6 address 19:1:1::4/64 and enable IS-IS IPv6 BFD on the interface.
On R2, enable BFD control-plane-independent failure detection for the IS-IS process (BFD C-bit support).
On R1, statically translate inside host 10.0.1.10 to global 203.0.113.1; mark Ethernet0/0 (10.0.1.1/24) as NAT inside and Ethernet0/1 (10.0.12.1/24) as NAT outside.

On R2, let inside users reach the Internet by PAT: define pool net-208 (203.0.113.129-203.0.113.158, mask 255.255.255.224), match inside subnet with ACL 1, overload it, and set Ethernet0/0 (10.0.12.2/24) inside and Ethernet0/1 (10.0.23.1/24) outside.
On R3, adjust the NAT translation timeouts: generic 300 s, UDP 300 s, DNS 45 s, TCP 2500 s, FIN/RST 45 s, ICMP 45 s, and SYN 45 s.
On R4, resolve an overlapping-address conflict with static inside-source NAT translating 10.0.40.10 to 203.0.113.33; Ethernet0/0 (10.0.14.2/24) is inside and Ethernet0/1 (10.0.24.2/24) is outside.

On R1, support outside-to-inside NAT using route maps: create pools POOL-A (203.0.113.4-6) and POOL-B (203.0.113.7-9), each with mask 255.255.255.128, and bind them with reversible route-map-based inside source translation (MAP-A and MAP-B).

On R2, configure NAT with stateful inter-chassis redundancy: pool VPN-18 (203.0.113.0-203.0.113.255, mask 255.255.255.0) and an inside source rule from ACL acl-18 using redundancy group 2 and mapping-id 152.

On R3, turn on NAT paired-address pooling, define pool net-208 (203.0.113.129-158, mask 255.255.255.240), match ACL 1 and overload, with Ethernet0/0 (10.0.23.2/24) inside and Ethernet0/1 (10.0.34.1/24) outside.

On R4, keep translations inside a single VRF: statically translate 10.0.40.10 to 203.0.113.1 in VRF vrf1 with match-in-vrf, and place Ethernet0/0 (10.0.14.2/24, inside) and Ethernet0/1 (10.0.24.2/24, outside) into vrf1.
On R1, export NAT translation records via high-speed logging using NetFlow v9 over UDP to collector 203.0.113.10 port 1020, sourced from Ethernet0/0.
On R1, create a multi-protocol VRF named VRF1 and enable its IPv6 address family.
On R2, define VRF vrf1 with route distinguisher 10:1 and both import and export route-target 10:1.
On R3, build a VASI interface pair so two VRFs can exchange traffic: vasileft 100 in VRF VRFLEFT (10.255.1.1/24) and vasiright 100 in VRF VRFRIGHT (10.255.2.1/24).
On R1, configure the global MPLS-TP identifiers: router-id 10.255.0.1 and global-id 1.
On R2, create a single-hop BFD template named mpls-bfd-1 with minimum transmit and receive intervals of 99 ms and a multiplier of 3.

On R3, build an MPLS-TP tunnel interface named tunnel 122 with 10000 kbps bandwidth, source 10.255.0.3 global-id 10, destination 10.255.0.1, BFD template mpls-tp-bfd-2, and working/protect LSPs (working in-label 111 out-label 112, protect in-label 100 out-label 113).

On R4, configure an MPLS-TP LSP at a midpoint between source 10.255.0.1 (global-id 2, tunnel-tp 4) and destination 10.255.0.3 (global-id 11, tunnel-tp 12), giving the forward and reverse LSPs 100 units of bandwidth and the labels/links shown.
On R1, enable MPLS forwarding (label switching) on interface Ethernet0/0.
On R2, reserve an MPLS static label range of 200-100000 with 16-199 set aside for static bindings, and create a static label binding mapping label 55 to prefix 10.0.0.0/8.
On R3, enable MLDP: turn on MLDP logging notifications and recursive forwarding.
On R4, build a GRE-over-IPv6 tunnel on Tunnel0: IPv6 address 3ffe:b00:c18:1::3/127, source Ethernet0/0, destination 2001:DB8:1111:2222::1, in GRE IPv6 mode.
On R1, adjust the MPLS LSP ping/traceroute compatibility settings: set the MPLS OAM echo revision to 4 and enable the echo vendor-extension.
On R2, prepare for EoMPLS by enabling IPv6 unicast routing, selecting LDP as the label protocol, and forcing the LDP router-id to come from Loopback0.

On R1, enable distributed IP multicast routing and PIM SSM with the default range; build extended ACL "mygroup" that denies IGMP from host 10.0.1.10 and permits all other IGMP; on Ethernet0/0 apply that ACL as the IGMP access-group, run PIM sparse mode, and force IGMP version 3.
On R2, define a multicast-flows class-map "static1" covering groups 232.1.1.7 through 232.1.1.20, and apply it on Ethernet0/0 as an IGMP static-group range.
On R3, enable IGMP SSM mapping without DNS lookups and add a static SSM map associating ACL 11 with source 10.0.2.10.
On R4, enable DNS-based IGMP SSM mapping: turn on SSM mapping with DNS query, set the multicast domain to ssm-map.cisco.com, and point to name server 203.0.113.53.
On R1 interface Ethernet0/0, statically forward multicast group 232.1.2.1 using the SSM map to resolve its source (ip igmp static-group with source ssm-map).
On R2 Tunnel100, create a static NHRP mapping from protocol address 10.255.10.2 to NBMA address 10.0.12.1, and map multicast traffic to NBMA 10.0.24.2.
On R3, enable IGMP snooping globally and also on bridge-domain 100.
On R4 interface Ethernet0/0, enable the IGMP unidirectional link feature so it can act as the upstream device for IGMP UDLR.
On R1 interface Ethernet0/0, apply the IPv6 access list named "inbound" to traffic entering the interface.
On R2, create an IPv6 access list "cisco" that permits host 2001:DB8:0:4::32 and denies host 2001:DB8:0:6::6, for use as vty access-class filtering.
On R3, create IPv6 access list "acl1" that denies traffic from 2001:DB8:0300:0201::/32 to 2001:DB8:1:1::/64 whose upper-layer protocol cannot be determined (undetermined-transport).
On R4, create IPv6 access list "hbh-acl" that first permits then denies ICMP traffic carrying a destination-options header (dest-option-type) for hop-by-hop filtering.
On R1, prepare a 6PE provider edge: enable IPv6 unicast routing and IPv6 CEF, then give Ethernet0/0 the source IPv6 address 2001:DB8:FFFF::2/64.
On R2, protect an IPv6 static route with BFDv6: create a static BFD neighbor reachable over Ethernet0/0 at 2001::1, then add the route 2001:DB8::/64 via that same interface and next hop.
On R3 interface Ethernet0/0, configure dual-stack addressing with IPv4 10.0.23.2/24 and IPv6 2001:db8::ffff:1/128, and bring it up.
On R4, create Loopback0 with IPv4 address 10.255.0.4/32 and IPv6 address 2001:db8::ffff:1/128.
On R1, build a multipoint GRE tunnel on Tunnel100: set GRE multipoint mode, tunnel key 3, and NHRP network-id 1.
On R2 Tunnel100, configure a PfRv3 Zero-SLA overlay path: 10000000 kbps bandwidth, IP 10.255.10.1/24, and domain path ISP1 with the zero-sla option.
On R3 Tunnel100, mark the domain path ISP1 as the path of last resort for PfRv3.
On R4 interface Ethernet0/0, lower the ARP cache entry expiration timeout to 30 seconds.
On R1 Port-channel1, require at least 1 active member link for the LACP bundle to come up (LACP min-bundle).
On R1, apply policy-based routing on Ethernet0/0 using route-map "equal-access", and define route-map "alpha" (permit 10) that matches ACL 1.
On R2, create route-map "abc" that makes its policy decision based on tracked object 2 (match track 2).
On R3, build route-map "policy_security" that, for source security group tag 100 sets next hop 10.0.23.1, and for destination security group tag 150 sets next hop 10.0.34.2.
On R4, define a route-tag list "list1" that permits 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.7, and a route-map "to-ospf" that matches that tag list.
On R1, create community-list 30 permitting community 100:190 and route-map "set_bucket" (permit 10) that matches it and sets traffic-index 2 for BGP policy accounting.
On R2, define the prefixes to import: ACL 50 permitting 10.0.1.0/24 and ip prefix-list "COLORADO" permitting 10.0.40.0/24.
On R3, filter ODR information with ACL 101 (permit host 10.0.2.10, deny 10.0.2.0/24, permit 10.0.0.0/8) applied inbound under the ODR routing process.
On R4, create route-map "additional_path1" (permit 10) that matches the best-3 additional-paths advertise-set and sets metric 500.
On R1 interface Ethernet0/0, configure an HSRP group named "mygroup" with virtual IP address 10.0.1.254.

On R2 interface Ethernet0/0 (10.0.12.2), make PIM aware of VRRP redundancy: enable VRRPv3, configure VRRP group 1 IPv4 with VRRS leader "VRRP1" and virtual IP 10.0.12.254, then bind PIM redundancy to VRRP1 with DR priority 90.

On R3, configure a redundancy application group 1 named "group1" (priority 100, failover threshold 50, preempt, track object 50 decrement 50) and a redundancy protocol 1 (hello 3 / hold 10, MD5 authentication key-string n1, BFD enabled).

On R4, configure mLACP inter-chassis redundancy group 50 monitored by BFD, with member peer IP 10.0.14.1, mLACP node-id 5, system-mac aa12.be45.d799, system-priority 100, and backbone interface Ethernet0/0.
On R1, configure the redundancy control-interface protocol: set redundancy mode none, then application redundancy protocol 4 named "rg1" with hello 3 / hold 10, text authentication, and BFD enabled.
On R2, create Port-channel10 with an LACP maximum bundle of 3 links and IP address 10.255.20.2/24.
On R3, build an 802.3ad EtherChannel: Port-channel1 with IP 10.255.20.3/24, and bundle Ethernet0/1 and Ethernet0/2 into it with channel-group 1 mode active.
On R4, create tracking object 100 that tracks the state of the Mobile IP home-agent application.
On R1, in GDOI group "gdoigroupone" tie the group member crypto state to tracked object 99 (client status active-sa track 99).

On R2 interface Ethernet0/1 (10.0.23.1/24, NAT outside), add a redundant NAT traffic interface: enable virtual reassembly, set redundancy RII 200, and join redundancy group 1 with virtual IP 10.0.23.200 (exclusive, decrement 10).
On R3, create the VXLAN NVE interface nve1 sourced from Loopback0, joining VNI 7115 to multicast group 225.1.1.1, and bring it up.

On R4 interface Ethernet0/2, configure a WAN traffic interface for an asymmetric-routing NAT design: IPv6 address 2001:DB8:2222::1/48, zone-member security z2, TCP MSS clamp 1360, redundancy RII 360, and enable redundancy asymmetric-routing.

On R1, enable Cisco TrustSec SXP with a default password "Cisco123", default source IP 10.255.0.1, a peer connection to 10.0.12.2 (password default, mode local both), speaker hold-time 950, and listener hold-time 750-1500.
On R2 interface Ethernet0/0, enable Cisco TrustSec role-based SGT caching for ingress traffic.
